advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fork-branch case to test_status_fold_replay_equivalence: trigger current_status mismatch with an incoming winning UUID carrying session/close_class and assert claimed_session/close_class fold on the fork winner.
evidence: _apply_status always passes a current that either matches state['status'] or is a normal transition: `_apply_status(state, "u1", "open", "in_progress", ...)` on a state already at status 'open' — so `current_status != state['status']` is false and only the else branch runs

Moved code documents a distinct fork-winner contract: `_fold_claimed_session(state, data)  # only when THIS (winning) event is applied` inside the `if not existing_uuid or incoming_uuid <= existing_uuid:` fork branch (src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py:127-128)

Pre-existing tests/unit/test_reducer_status_fork_record.py:49-55 crafts a fork STATUS event with `{"status": "closed", "current_status": "in_progress"}` but only asserts status_fork_resolutions recording; it does not carry session/close_class data nor assert the fork-winner folds fired
advisory.finding: The replay-equivalence oracle for the moved process_status only drives the non-fork (else) branch; the fork branch (current_status != state['status']) — which re-invokes the three moved folds on the fork-WINNER path and populates status_fork_resolutions — is never exercised by this test, so a regression in the fork-branch fold application introduced by the move (e.g. dropping the winner-only _fold_claimed_session/_fold_close_metadata call) would not be caught here.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop or rework test_both_modules_under_the_size_target — rely on the single-sourced module-size gate rather than a hardcoded 650-line count assertion in this test.
evidence: `n = len(Path(mod.__file__).read_text().splitlines()); assert n <= 650` — asserts file length, not behavior
tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py:43-51 already enforces the absolute cap for all src/rebar modules via the CI single-source limit (read_limit / compute_over_cap_modules)
The 650 threshold is a locally-invented sub-cap not tied to the single-sourced limit; a behavior-preserving comment addition pushing the file to 651 lines fails this test with no behavioral change
advisory.finding: test_both_modules_under_the_size_target asserts a raw line count (<=650) against each module file; this is a change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving edit (adding comments or blank lines) with no observable-behavior change, and duplicates the absolute cap already enforced by test_module_size_contract.py from the single-sourced .github/module-size-limit.txt.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the ast.Import branch to assert the exact bare-module names rather than a substring heuristic.
evidence: tests/unit/test_processors_status_split.py:54:                assert "._processors" not in alias.name or "_status" in alias.name
dropped.finding: The one-way-import guard's `ast.Import` branch uses a loose substring heuristic (`"._processors" not in alias.name or "_status" in alias.name`) that would wrongly pass a hypothetical `import rebar.reducer._processors_identity` or any other module whose dotted name lacks `._processors`, and could mis-classify future sibling modules; the ImportFrom branch is exact but the Import branch is fragile.
scenarios: A future edit adds `import rebar.reducer._processors` (bare) — caught; but an `import ...._processors_something_else` slips through the `_status` allowance if it contains the substring.
